name: Tapetal cell (dog)
blurb: A dog's tapetal cell: a flat, many-sided cell in the shiny layer behind the retina, its cytoplasm filled with slender zinc-rich rods that bounce light back.
note: Model: a tapetal cell of the dog's eye (Canis lupus familiaris), cut in half. Measured in dogs: the tapetum is up to 20 cells thick where thickest and 20 to 70 µm thick; its cells hold slender electron-dense rods in a regular array; the rods of normal beagles contain zinc and cysteine. Measured in the cat: rodlet length about 5 µm, diameter 100 to 230 nm, cell thickness 3 to 4 µm. The dog study says the dog's rodlets are similar in size to the cat's, but more closely packed and less well lined up. No dog figure for cell thickness was found, so the cat thickness stands in for it. Illustrative: the width of the cell, its nucleus, the rodlet count and directions, and the colours. The cells above and below show faintly.

tapetum_thickness.note: mean of the thickest part of the tapetum, standard deviation 17 µm, range 20 to 70 µm, in the histological part of the study (a subset of the 53 dogs; the paper gives 20 cases); the layer thins towards its edge

cell_thickness.calc: midpoint of the 3 to 4 µm given for the flat cells of the cat tapetum; no dog figure was found
cell_thickness.note: cat value used as a stand-in for the dog

width.note: illustrative; no source opened gives the width of a dog tapetal cell

rodlet_length.note: cat; the dog's rodlets are about the same size as the cat's (lesiuk1983)

rodlet_diameter.note: cat; reported as 100 nm in some studies, 100 to 120 and 190 to 230 nm in others

rodlet_spacing.note: cat, centre to centre; 150 or 400 nm in different reports. The dog's rodlets are more closely packed than the cat's (lesiuk1983)

volume_fraction.note: illustrative; the nucleus of a dog tapetal cell was not measured in any source opened

count.calc: a hexagonal lattice of 100 nm rods 150 nm apart fills 0.907 x (0.1/0.15)^2 = 0.40 of the space; a 5 µm rod of 0.1 µm diameter has a volume of 0.039 µm³; 0.40 / 0.039 = 10.3 rods per µm³; the cell is about 1750 µm³ (a six-sided cell 24 µm across and 3.5 µm thick), and 90% of it is taken as rod-bearing (illustrative): about 16,000

granules.note: drawn as rods 3 µm long, shorter than the 5 µm measured in the cat, so that they lie inside a cell only 3.5 µm thick when drawn in random directions

not_drawn: the capillaries of the choroid beneath the layer

special.note: Slender, electron-dense rods lie in a regular array in the cytoplasm of dog tapetal cells (yamaue2014); the rods are rich in zinc (wen1982). In life they lie side by side in bundles parallel to the plane of the layer (cat, zueva2022); here 700 are drawn in random directions, an illustrative simplification.

cut: The cell is cut in half through its thickness: a flat slab with the oval nucleus in it and slender rods filling the cytoplasm around the nucleus; the cells of the layers above and below show faintly.

colours.convention: Cell membrane pale green, the inside dark; rodlets bright pale green because they are what reflects light; nucleus violet. All of it is a code: the real tapetum shines blue-green to yellow in a torch beam, but the colour of a single rod is not shown by this picture.

cytosol.name: Cytosol
cytosol.about: The watery inside of the cell. In a tapetal cell the rods take much of it.

granule.name: Reflecting rodlet
granule.about: A slender rod rich in zinc and cysteine. Its inner make-up is shown as a protein stand-in when the picture goes down.

about: The tapetum lucidum of a dog lies in the choroid behind the retina. Where it is thickest it is up to 20 cells deep, and it averaged 53 µm thick in a study of dogs. Light that passes the retina meets these cells and is sent back through it.
The cell here is a flat six-sided slab, 24 µm across and 3.5 µm thick. The thickness is the cat value; the width is illustrative. Its volume works out to {drawn.cellVolume} µm³.

The rods are real structures, long and thin, packed side by side. {drawn.granules} of the about 16,000 estimated are drawn, in random directions; in the eye they lie parallel to the layer. In the dog they are packed more closely than in the cat and are less well lined up.

Not drawn: mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum and the Golgi apparatus, whose size in these cells is not known from the sources used; the junctions between neighbours; and the capillaries beneath the layer. The nucleus is a single illustrative oval.

yamaue2014.cite: Yamaue Y, Hosaka YZ, Uehara M (2014) Macroscopic and histological variations in the cellular tapetum in dogs. J Vet Med Sci 76(8):1099-1103
yamaue2014.used_for: up to 20 layers of tapetal cells; thickness 20 to 70 µm, mean 53 ± 17 µm in the histological subset of a 53-dog study (20 cases); slender electron-dense rods in a regular array; brick-like layers

lesiuk1983.cite: Lesiuk TP, Braekevelt CR (1983) Fine structure of the canine tapetum lucidum. J Anat 136:157-164 (abstract)
lesiuk1983.used_for: dog rodlets are about the size of the cat's, more closely packed and less precisely oriented

zueva2022.cite: Zueva L et al. (2022) Multilayer subwavelength gratings or sandwiches with periodic structure shape light reflection in the tapetum lucidum of taxonomically diverse vertebrate animals. J Biophotonics 15(6):e202200002
zueva2022.used_for: cat tapetal cells: 3 to 4 µm thick, rodlets about 5 µm long, 100 nm or more in diameter, 150 to 400 nm apart, in a hexagonal lattice, in bundles parallel to the choroid

wen1982.cite: Wen GY, Sturman JA, Wisniewski HM, MacDonald A, Niemann WH (1982) Chemical and ultrastructural changes in tapetum of beagles with a hereditary abnormality. Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 23(6):733-742 (abstract)
wen1982.used_for: tapetal rods of normal beagles hold zinc and cysteine; beagles with a hereditary tapetal abnormality lacked both
